title: discrete hypothesis points in module-reuse structure space
hypothesis: When new tasks use one of eight reusable module recombination rules, selecting a discrete hypothesis from a small codebook can preserve heldout function quality with fewer support examples than continuous task-code fitting and fewer inference bytes than independent task coefficients.
physical_object: Eight fixed nonlinear shared modules and eight learned recombination rule prototypes
mirror_coordinate: One uint8 hypothesis address selecting among eight module coefficient vectors
logical_multiplicity: Eight candidate recombination hypotheses over the same shared module bank
controls: continuous rank-2 PCA code fit from support

development.selection_metric: No hyperparameter tuning; confirm frozen implementation and byte/quality accounting only.

world.modules: Eight fixed nonlinear functions phi_j(x)=tanh(w_j dot x+b_j), newly drawn per world
world.rules: Eight equally spaced angular points in a two-dimensional coefficient plane, mapped through a world-specific orthonormal 2x8 module basis; each prototype has a distinct uint8 address
world.training: For each prototype, fit its coefficient vector from three independent 128-example training tasks; learn continuous rank-2 PCA structure only from those 24 training tasks
world.heldout: Sixteen new task instances uniformly choose a prototype with independent support/test examples; no heldout labels, indices, support observations, or outputs enter prototype fitting
world.noise: Gaussian target noise sigma 0.03; primary function error measured against noiseless target

policy.discrete_mirror: Choose the prototype with minimum support prediction MSE and store its uint8 address
policy.native_codebook: Identical nearest-prototype inference over the same serialized coefficient table
policy.continuous: Fit two PCA coordinates from support and decode through the learned rank-2 basis
policy.random: Nearest support fit among eight random coefficient prototypes
policy.independent: Least-squares fit of eight coefficients directly from support
policy.quality: Heldout mean squared function error, per-world mean and worst heldout task
policy.support_efficiency: Smallest preregistered shot count meeting MSE <= .0025 in every fresh world; report full curve

storage.authority: Actual deterministic payload bytes using little-endian float32/int32 and uint8 code IDs
paid_objects: eight prototype coefficient vectors or continuous rank-2 basis
one uint8 address or two float32 task coordinates per heldout task
storage.amortization: Charge shared objects once across 16 heldout tasks and all task-specific codes; also report per-task amortized bytes
storage.excluded: No learned prototype, codebook, index or reconstruction state is free.

success_gate: At no more than four support examples, discrete selection reaches MSE <= .0025 in every fresh world and costs at least 20% fewer total 16-task payload bytes than independent coefficients. Mirror-specific gain additionally requires beating native nearest-codebook inference at matched bytes/compute.
failure_gate: Quality/byte gate misses or exact alias to native codebook/rule selection fails Mirror-specific attribution. Preserve any few-shot utility result separately.
boundaries: Synthetic nonlinear module bank only; not an RL or neural-network benchmark.
Heldout task instances choose among learned prototypes; unseen recombination rules are not tested.
No claim that eight code addresses equal eight independent experts or independent capacity.
Only a single module bank with eight candidates and 16 heldout tasks is screened.
